## Scope

CHORALE first expresses every modality on a fixed vocabulary of named
biological concepts. It then estimates concept-level phenotype effects,
concept-family effects, a low-rank joint representation of the stacked concept
scores, held-out transfer of those directions, and phenotype-linked free
dimensions outside the vocabulary. These are separate estimands sharing one
encoding, not interchangeable versions of one result.

A concept is a set of features defined before results are inspected. The
modalities are measured on different individuals, so the vocabulary supplies a
common reference frame; no individual-level cross-modality profile is observed
or reconstructed.

Notation is introduced where it is used. Modalities are indexed by \(m\), concepts by \(c\), samples
within modality \(m\) by \(i\), and features of modality \(m\) by \(j\).

## The vocabulary and its coverage

A vocabulary is a collection of sets \(\mathcal{C}_c\) of feature identifiers. For modality \(m\)
these become a feature-by-concept weight matrix \(W_m\), whose entry \(w_{jc}\) is the weight with
which feature \(j\) carries concept \(c\). A gene or protein identifier matching \(n\) identifiers
in the reference space contributes \(1/n\) to each, so a one-to-many map contributes proportionally
rather than counting once per match. A lipid species carries a concept when its class takes part in
the pathway that names the concept.

Modality \(m\) expresses concept \(c\) when \(\#\{j : w_{jc} > 0\}\) reaches a declared minimum. The
counts are reported per concept and per modality, since a concept a modality cannot express carries
no evidence there.

## Concept scores

Let \(X_m\) be the samples-by-features matrix of modality \(m\) after the per-modality transform,
centred and scaled by feature. The concept score matrix is

\[
S_m = X_m \tilde{W}_m , \qquad
\tilde{w}_{jc} = \frac{w_{jc}}{\sum_{j'} w_{j'c}},
\]

so each score is a weighted mean of standardised feature values and a large concept and a small one
are on one scale. Columns of \(S_m\) are standardised afterwards, so an effect on one concept is
comparable with an effect on another.

The design does not enter this step. Scoring therefore cannot be shaped by the contrast the scores
are subsequently tested on.

## Free dimensions

Curated concepts overlap, so the columns of \(S_m\) are correlated and the coefficients of a
regression on them are close to arbitrary. What the overlap does not make arbitrary is the space the
scores span, and it is that space which decides what is left over. The residual is therefore taken
against the orthogonal projection onto that span,

\[
R_m = X_m - S_m S_m^{+} X_m ,
\]

with \(S_m^{+}\) the Moore-Penrose inverse. Then \(S_m^{T} R_m = 0\) exactly, so a free dimension
cannot carry concept signal by construction rather than by approximation.

Independent component analysis of \(R_m\) gives free scores \(F_m\) and free loadings \(B_m\) with
\(R_m \approx F_m B_m^{T}\). The share of variance each channel holds is reported as
\(1 - \lVert R_m\rVert_F^2 / \lVert X_m\rVert_F^2\) for the concepts and
\((\lVert R_m\rVert_F^2 - \lVert R_m - F_m B_m^{T}\rVert_F^2) / \lVert X_m\rVert_F^2\) for the free
dimensions.

## How many free dimensions

The count is selected by reproducibility. At each candidate count \(k\) the decomposition is run
from several initialisations and on several subsamples of the samples. Components of every run are
matched one to one against a reference run by absolute correlation of loadings, solved as a linear
assignment problem, and the matched correlation is recorded per component. Loadings rather than
scores are compared, because a run on a subsample has no scores for the samples it left out.

The selected count is the largest \(k\) such that every count up to and including it has its weakest
component above a declared threshold. Two bounds cap the search. Parallel analysis on \(R_m\),
comparing observed eigenvalues with those of column-permuted data, gives the first. A cap of one
component per five samples gives the second, since beyond it the recovered axes describe individual
samples.

Where the realised concept-score matrix has full row rank on the centred sample
space, its projection is the identity on that space and \(R_m = 0\) up to
numerical precision. Having at least as many concepts as samples makes full row
rank possible, but does not guarantee it: correlated or redundant concept
scores can have lower rank. CHORALE therefore decides from the residual norm,
not from the dimensions alone. No free dimensions are fitted when that residual
is numerical dust.

## Adjusted design effects

For concept \(c\) in modality \(m\), let \(y_{mc}\) be its score vector. CHORALE fits

\[
y_{mc} = D_m \beta_{mc} + \varepsilon_{mc},
\]

where \(D_m\) carries an intercept, the phenotype contrasts, and every covariate the modalities
share and can jointly estimate. Continuous covariates enter as standardised slopes; a categorical
covariate enters as treatment contrasts on the levels every modality realises, so a level observed
in one cohort and not another cannot enter the comparison. The reported phenotype coefficient is
adjusted for the rest of \(D_m\).

A covariate absent from a modality, incompatible in type or levels, more than half missing, or not
jointly estimable after the covariates already retained is excluded with its reason recorded.

## Combining the modalities

Let \(b_{mc}\) be the phenotype coefficient for concept \(c\) in modality \(m\) and \(s_{mc}\) its
standard error, over the modalities \(M_c\) that express the concept. The combination is
inverse-variance weighted,

\[
\hat{b}_c = \frac{\sum_{m \in M_c} b_{mc}/s_{mc}^2}{\sum_{m \in M_c} 1/s_{mc}^2},
\qquad
\hat{s}_c = \Big(\sum_{m \in M_c} 1/s_{mc}^2\Big)^{-1/2},
\qquad
Z_c = \hat{b}_c / \hat{s}_c .
\]

A modality that measures the concept precisely counts for more than one that measures it loosely,
and effects in opposite directions cancel, so a concept the modalities disagree about cannot reach a
large statistic by accumulating disagreement. Cochran's
\(Q_c = \sum_{m} (b_{mc} - \hat{b}_c)^2 / s_{mc}^2\), read against \(\chi^2_{|M_c| - 1}\), reports
whether the modalities are describing one quantity, and the share of modalities agreeing in sign
with \(\hat{b}_c\) is reported beside it.

No correspondence between modalities is estimated at any point. That is what the fixed vocabulary
removes from the problem.

## Calibration and error control

The quantity under test is the phenotype coefficient of a model that also carries the adjusting
covariates, so the null must be a null for that coefficient. Shuffling raw phenotype labels would
break its relation to those covariates as well, giving designs the study could not have produced.

The null is therefore the one of Freedman and Lane (1983). Write \(D_m = [Z_m, P_m]\), with \(Z_m\)
the intercept and the adjusting covariates and \(P_m\) the phenotype contrasts. The reduced model
\(y_{mc} = Z_m\gamma_{mc} + r_{mc}\) is fitted, its residuals are permuted, and the response is
rebuilt as

\[
y^{*}_{mc} = Z_m\hat{\gamma}_{mc} + \Pi r_{mc},
\]

with \(\Pi\) a permutation matrix. The full model is refitted to \(y^{*}_{mc}\) and its phenotype
coefficient recorded. The design matrix never changes, so the phenotype keeps exactly the relation
to the covariates it has in the data, and only the part of the score the covariates do not explain
is exchanged. The same \(\Pi\) is applied to every concept of a modality, so the correlation between
concepts that share features is carried into the null rather than assumed away.

\(\Pi\) is unrestricted unless the study declares which samples are exchangeable. Blocks are read
only from the columns named in `chorale_control(exchangeability_blocks = )`, because a repeated
measure, a litter or a processing batch is a fact about the study. Blocks are not inferred from the
design. A continuous covariate would give one sample per block, and the permutation would then be
either the identity, or a permutation over covariates dropped until it is not. Neither is a
statement about the study.

The encoder is never refitted: \(S_m\) is computed once and only its response is rebuilt. The number
of permutations \(B\) is therefore set by the resolution required rather than by what a refit can
afford, and the smallest attainable p-value is \(1/(B+1)\).

Two quantities come from the same permutations. Writing \(Z^{(b)}_c\) for the statistic of concept
\(c\) under permutation \(b\),

\[
p_c = \frac{1 + \#\{b : |Z^{(b)}_c| \ge |Z_c|\}}{B+1},
\qquad
p^{\text{fam}}_c = \frac{1 + \#\{b : \max_{c'} |Z^{(b)}_{c'}| \ge |Z_c|\}}{B+1}.
\]

The second controls the family-wise error rate over the vocabulary, exactly under the dependence
that overlapping concepts have, because the permutations carry the same overlap the data do. The
false discovery rate at threshold \(t\) is estimated from the same array as

\[
\widehat{\mathrm{FDR}}(t) = \frac{B^{-1}\#\{(b,c') : |Z^{(b)}_{c'}| \ge t\}}{\#\{c' : |Z_{c'}| \ge t\}} .
\]

Each concept's q-value is the smallest such estimate over thresholds that would also call it, which
makes the reported rates monotone in the statistic.

Free dimensions are calibrated the same way, with the maximum taken over free dimensions rather than
over concepts, so the two families are controlled separately and neither borrows the other's null.

The modality shuffle is reported as a description rather than as a test. Three differences separate a shuffled
collection from the fit. Pooling keeps only the features the modalities share, so the shuffled
collection is scored on a smaller feature space and often on a smaller vocabulary. The reallocation
preserves neither each modality's sample count nor its design composition. The observed statistic
was computed on the full assays. No error rate follows from that comparison.

## Concept families

Let \(G_g\) be a family fixed from vocabulary overlap before testing. Complete
linkage at Jaccard threshold \(a\) ensures that every pair in a multi-concept
family overlaps by at least \(a\). Ungrouped concepts remain singletons.

For one phenotype term, the family statistic is

\[
T_g = \frac{\left|\sum_{c \in G_g} Z_c\right|}{\sqrt{|G_g|}}.
\]

The signed sum makes concordant concepts accumulate and discordant concepts
cancel. For permutation \(b\), the same function is applied to the signed
statistics \(Z_c^{(b)}\) already generated for concept inference. This retains
dependence induced by shared features. `p_value` compares a family with its own
null; `p_family` compares it with the largest family statistic in each
permutation; `q_value` estimates FDR over families. A supported family is a
group-level result and does not imply that each member is supported.

## Joint low-rank state

Concept meta-analysis combines scalar effects estimated separately. Joint-state
analysis instead factorises all concept-score observations at once. Let \(Z_m\)
contain the scores of modality \(m\), after optional regression on
modality-local nuisance variables and centring and scaling each concept within
that modality. The blocks are stacked by row to form \(Z\). Let \(\Omega\) mark
the entries that were observed; a modality-concept combination below the
coverage threshold is missing, not zero.

For rank \(k\), `chorale_joint_state()` alternates ridge-regularised
least-squares updates for sample scores \(U\) and concept loadings \(V\), using
only \(\Omega_{ic}=1\):

\[
\sum_{(i,c):\Omega_{ic}=1} (Z_{ic} - u_i^T v_c)^2.
\]

The small ridge makes each update solvable even when a row or column has fewer
observations than components. Zero-filled singular vectors initialise the
algorithm, but unobserved entries never enter its update objective. Automatic
component selection currently applies reproducibility selection to the
zero-filled stacked matrix; where coverage differs sharply, inspect that
selection and compare prespecified counts.

After convergence, a rotation orders the fitted rank-one terms by the variance
they carry. This does not make the factors unique: \(UV^T\) is the fitted
reconstruction, and signs, rotations, or nearly equivalent low-rank solutions
can describe similar data. The component share is the squared norm of its
rank-one approximation over observed entries divided by the observed squared
score norm. With missing entries these shares need not form an exact partition,
because cross-terms over the observation mask may remain.

Stacking increases the number and diversity of observed rows and allows each
concept to contribute wherever it is measured. It does not identify a direction
merely because the vocabulary dimension exceeds one modality's sample count.

## Evidence for a joint component

For each component score, CHORALE fits a stacked linear model containing an
intercept, modality, the phenotype terms, and covariates shared across
modalities. The modality term absorbs cohort-level composition differences.
Per-modality models are reported separately as descriptions.

Calibration again uses Freedman--Lane residual permutation, but exchange is
always restricted within modality in addition to declared blocks. The
component-specific p-value, max-component family-wise p-value, and
permutation-based q-value have the same definitions as in the concept branch,
with components replacing concepts.

Component orientation is arbitrary. Multiplying its scores and loadings by -1
reverses the effect sign but leaves the reconstruction and two-sided inference
unchanged. Declare an orientation from loadings or an external convention before
describing a component effect as positive or negative.

## Leave-one-modality-out transfer

For held-out modality \(h\), the state is fitted on all \(m \ne h\). Let
\(Z_h^{(C)}\) contain the held-out scores for concepts also present in training
loadings \(V^{(C)}\). Projection uses

\[
U_h = Z_h^{(C)} V^{(C)}
      \left(V^{(C)T}V^{(C)} + 10^{-8}I\right)^{-1}.
\]

The projected scores are tested in the held-out design with Freedman--Lane
permutations. At least three modalities are required so the training set remains
joint. The returned `p_value` is component-specific, not max-statistic or FDR
control over the transfer table.

Each held-out fit has independent sign and order. Its loadings are matched
one-to-one to a full-data reference by the assignment maximising absolute
loading correlation. `component` is the reference label,
`fitted_component` the local label, and `loading_agreement` the signed
correlation. The reference supplies labels only. Effect signs from different
held-out fits are comparable only after accounting for orientation.

## Attribution among overlapping concepts

Concepts sharing features are not independent claims. For each concept, those whose Jaccard overlap
with it in the measured features of a modality reaches a declared threshold are regressed out of its
score, and the effect is re-estimated. The result is reported beside the original. A concept whose
statistic survives carries the signal itself; one whose statistic collapses describes the
neighbourhood it sits in.

## Recovery against a known correspondence

Where two modalities were measured on the same individuals, the pairing can be withheld and used
afterwards to check what the vocabulary asserts. The two modalities are presented under their own
sample identifiers and encoded as though disjoint. The pairing then enters once, to compute the
concept-by-concept agreement matrix \(A\) with \(a_{cd} = \mathrm{cor}(S_{A,c}, S_{B,d})\) across
the individuals both were measured on.

The correlation is signed. A concept score has a fixed orientation, since a larger score means a
larger weighted mean of the features carrying the concept, so two modalities that rank the same
biological state in opposite directions have not recovered it. Sign indeterminacy belongs to the
free dimensions, which are not what is compared here.

Three quantities frame the result. The paired upper bound is the mean agreement of the optimal
assignment of \(A\), which is what any method knowing the pairing could reach. The random baseline
is the mean agreement over one-to-one relabellings drawn at random. The recovery is the mean of the
diagonal of \(A\), the identity the vocabulary asserts, concept for concept by name, computed
without a paired sample having been seen.

Random alignment is a baseline and not a bound: a vocabulary whose names do not track the same
biology in the two modalities places below it, and the reported placement is negative rather than
clipped.

## Conditions of applicability

The vocabulary bounds what the concept channel expresses. Biology absent from it appears only in the
free dimensions, and is named there by loadings rather than identified.

A concept expressible in two modalities and not in a third yields evidence across two. Coverage is
reported per concept for that reason.

Curated concepts overlap, so attribution requires the overlap structure to be carried through the
inference, which is what the family-wise permutation and the neighbour-adjusted statistic do.

ICA free dimensions rely on stable non-Gaussian structure. `chorale_gates()`
reports non-Gaussianity and modality-difference diagnostics, read on the same
transformed scale the encoder consumes, but a diagnostic passing is not proof
that an individual free axis is identified.

A coordinated phenotype shift supports an association with the named concept.
Ordering cause and consequence requires timing, mediation or perturbation.

## Literature

Independent component analysis and its identification conditions follow Comon (1994) and Hyvärinen
and Oja (2000); the FastICA implementation is Marchini, Heaton and Ripley's `fastICA`. Parallel
analysis is Horn (1965). Linear assignment for matching components across runs uses the Hungarian
algorithm through `clue` (Hornik 2005). Inverse-variance combination and Cochran's Q are standard
fixed-effect meta-analysis, as in Borenstein et al. (2009). The permutation null for a coefficient
in a model carrying nuisance covariates is Freedman and Lane (1983), whose behaviour under the
general linear model is reviewed by Winkler et al. (2014). Permutation-based false discovery
estimation follows Tusher, Tibshirani and Chu (2001) and Storey and Tibshirani (2003); max-statistic
family-wise control follows Westfall and Young (1993). Single-sample set scoring by the mean
standardised level of a set's members is the construction underlying Lee et al. (2008) and
Hänzelmann, Castelo and Guinney (2013). Lipid shorthand names are parsed with Goslin (Kopczynski et
al. 2020).

The observed-entry joint fit is an alternating regularised low-rank
approximation. A reconstruction can be stable while a particular factor basis
is not unique. The transfer analysis is a held-out assessment of the
implemented fitted directions, not a separate identifiability theorem.
